recommendation.summary: Use native UIs for their own mapped sessions; keep the orchestrator ledger authoritative across harnesses.
recommendation.reference_text_proposed: Use each harness UI only as a watch surface for sessions the harness can map and display. Claude's Agent View is CLI/TUI; its Desktop session sidebar is separate. Kiro Agent Focus documents in-place replies for Kiro IDE sessions; Crew state and usage views apply to Crew sessions. Antigravity App Overview follows subagents, while documented approval-jump controls are CLI-only. Codex app imports CLI/IDE session history and has eligible per-chat usage, but may omit delegated work. Keep the orchestrator ledger authoritative for cross-harness state, questions, approvals, and usage until an exact worker-to-native-session mapping is demonstrated.

retention_and_cleanup.native_session_histories: The five #162-owned histories named in the receipt remain untouched and retained because UI inspection was unavailable. Parent owns any future targeted disposition. No shared DB or telemetry was accessed.
retention_and_cleanup.generated_app_data: No app data was extracted or inspected. Kiro Crew may have written routine app data when launched. Its root process remained open after the capture attempt and was not closed because CUA returned no usable accessibility/screenshot surface; no session was changed.

limitations: No local GUI showed any of the five #162 histories; all documented controls are not local observations.
The Codex app UI was not automated because the computer-use policy forbids it; no Codex app API metadata was used as a substitute for GUI evidence.
No source found establishes arbitrary external headless-worker adoption across all candidate UIs; absence of documentation does not prove impossibility.

Usage eligibility is account-dependent for Codex. Kiro Crew usage evidence is for 0.9.0 and is mismatched to the locally recorded 0.11.1. Kiro Agent Focus and Antigravity app usage details were not specified by the inspected pages.
